note: Rows published automatically by the weekend pipeline before editor review. Same columns as the sheet plus Auto=1. Rows move to the sheet once reviewed; the sheet wins on ID clashes.

rows.EpisodeTitle: Anthropic Goes Public, Nvidia in Crisis, Markets Tank, Open Source Crackdown?
rows.Speaker: Jason Calacanis
rows.Quote: They hit a $2 trillion valuation, raised over $107 billion, green shoe filled.
rows.Claim: Anthropic's IPO valued it at $2tn and raised over $107bn, beating SpaceX's $85bn IPO.
rows.Evidence: Anthropic priced an upsized IPO at $83 a share (above the $70-78 range): 980M shares for $81.3bn, plus a $26bn concurrent private placement, $107.3bn in all. That is the largest IPO on record; SpaceX raised $75bn in its June 2026 base deal and $85.7bn with the over-allotment. But the valuation at the IPO price was about $1.38tn fully diluted (other reports: about $1.5tn), and at the first-day close of $97.17 it was about $1.28tn on shares outstanding, not $2tn. Whether the greenshoe (up to 147M shares) was exercised had not been disclosed.
rows.Notes: The $107bn and the record are right. The $2tn valuation overstates it by roughly a third, and he uses it later (16:16, 20:36) to argue Anthropic trades at 20-30x revenue, so the number matters. Same deal as row 13 (Friedberg).

rows.EpisodeTitle: Anthropic Goes Public, Nvidia in Crisis, Markets Tank, Open Source Crackdown?
rows.Speaker: Chamath Palihapitiya
rows.Quote: The stock was up 8% or 9% at one point for buying an AI company.
rows.Claim: Palo Alto Networks stock jumped 8-9% because it bought an AI (open-weight model) company.
rows.Evidence: PANW announced the $4.5bn all-stock purchase of Applied Compute (a platform for post-training and serving open-weight models) on 18 Nov 2026, together with its fiscal Q1 results: revenue up 39% to $3.44bn, an EPS beat and raised FY2027 guidance. Shares rose about 9% after hours and more than 9% pre-market on 19 Nov. Arora said the model training and inference business 'could be bigger than what we do today'.
rows.Notes: The 8-9% move is right, but it came on the same release as an earnings beat and a guidance raise; reports attribute it to both. Presenting it as the market rewarding the acquisition alone omits that (rule 4).

rows.EpisodeTitle: Anthropic Goes Public, Nvidia in Crisis, Markets Tank, Open Source Crackdown?
rows.Speaker: Jason Calacanis
rows.Quote: They authorized $150 billion in additional buybacks back in September before Jensen was ousted. Total buybacks $235 billion.
rows.Claim: In September Nvidia authorized an extra $150bn of buybacks, taking the total to $235bn.
rows.Evidence: On 28 Sep 2026 Nvidia's board added $150bn to its repurchase program, 'increasing the total remaining amount authorized to $235 billion', to be executed through fiscal 2028; the release called it the largest increase in history.
rows.Notes: $235bn is the remaining authorization, not buybacks done. The release quotes Huang, not the CFO; the CFO remark ('now's the time') was not found.

rows.EpisodeTitle: Anthropic Goes Public, Nvidia in Crisis, Markets Tank, Open Source Crackdown?
rows.Speaker: Jason Calacanis
rows.Quote: The market wasn't allowed to do big M&A. That was off the table during Biden. Now it's back on the table for Trump.
rows.Claim: Big M&A was off the table under Biden and is back under Trump.
rows.Evidence: Biden's FTC and DOJ were more aggressive: they brought a record 50 merger enforcement actions in FY2022 and 29 litigated challenges in 2021-24 (27 in Trump's first term). But big deals still closed, including Microsoft-Activision ($69bn) after the FTC lost its injunction bid, and the share of reported deals challenged stayed at or below 1.55% each year, lower than any year since 2007.
rows.Notes: Tougher scrutiny under Biden is real; 'not allowed' and 'off the table' overstate it.

rows.EpisodeTitle: Anthropic Goes Public, Nvidia in Crisis, Markets Tank, Open Source Crackdown?
rows.Speaker: Jason Calacanis
rows.Quote: if you look at companies like Microsoft, they were at, I think, $900,000 an employee, and now they're trending towards $2 million per employee.
rows.Claim: Microsoft's revenue per employee has risen from about $900k toward $2m.
rows.Evidence: Microsoft's revenue per employee was about $929k in FY2022 and about $1.49m in FY2026 ($331.8bn revenue, about 223,000 staff at 30 June 2026).
rows.Notes: Single secondary source computing from 10-K figures. 'Trending towards $2 million' is a direction, not a current figure; the rise is about 60% in four years.

rows.EpisodeTitle: Anthropic Goes Public, Nvidia in Crisis, Markets Tank, Open Source Crackdown?
rows.Speaker: Jason Calacanis
rows.Quote: According to Reuters, companies could soon be forced to disclose on their websites if they're using Chinese open-source AI models.
rows.Claim: Reuters reports the administration is weighing a rule forcing companies to disclose Chinese AI model use on their websites; Airbnb, DoorDash and Cursor got House China committee letters this year.
rows.Evidence: Reuters reported on 18 Nov 2026 that Treasury and the White House OSTP have discussed requiring US companies such as Airbnb to disclose their use of Chinese AI models on their websites; it was not clear whether the idea was gaining traction. The House China and Homeland Security committees wrote to Airbnb and Anysphere (Cursor) in April 2026 and to DoorDash in July 2026 over their use of Qwen and Kimi.
rows.Notes: He also says Bessent is driving it; Reuters names Treasury and OSTP, not Bessent personally.

rows.EpisodeTitle: Anthropic Goes Public, Nvidia in Crisis, Markets Tank, Open Source Crackdown?
rows.Speaker: Jason Calacanis
rows.Quote: He bought Hugging Face and he bought Poolside. He spent 20 billion on those two companies.
rows.Claim: Under Huang, Nvidia spent about $20bn buying open-source AI assets Hugging Face and Poolside.
rows.Evidence: Nvidia agreed on 2 Sep 2026 to buy Hugging Face for $12.93bn. On 21 Aug 2026 it paid Poolside $6bn to license its model-building software, hired 109 staff and invested $1bn. Together about $19.9bn.
rows.Notes: Poolside was not bought: Poolside's investor letter says the deal is 'not an acquisition'. The total and the point (a big bet on open models) stand.

rows.EpisodeTitle: Anthropic Goes Public, Nvidia in Crisis, Markets Tank, Open Source Crackdown?
rows.Speaker: Jason Calacanis
rows.Quote: They've shed $2 trillion in market cap in the last 30 days, down 35%. Two weeks since Jensen got shivved, it's down 20%.
rows.Claim: Nvidia has lost about $2tn (35%) in recent weeks, and about 20% since the scandal broke.
rows.Evidence: Nvidia's all-time closing high was $239.24 on 6 Oct 2026. It closed at $150.96 on 18 Nov (market cap $3.64tn), about 37% lower and roughly $2tn below the peak. It closed at $186.64 on 6 Nov, the day of the NYT spy report, so the fall since then is about 19%.
rows.Notes: The peak was about six weeks before taping, not 30 days. The 19 Nov price was not confirmed.

rows.EpisodeTitle: Anthropic Goes Public, Nvidia in Crisis, Markets Tank, Open Source Crackdown?
rows.Speaker: Jason Calacanis
rows.Quote: Revenue and net profit both doubled. Yes, doubled on already absurdly large numbers to $116 billion and $65 billion respectively.
rows.Claim: Nvidia's quarterly revenue and net profit doubled to $116bn and $65bn, yet the stock fell.
rows.Evidence: Nvidia's Q3 FY2027 (to 25 Oct 2026) revenue was $115.8bn, up 103% from $57.0bn; GAAP net income $65.3bn, up from $31.9bn. Shares closed 0.4% lower on 17 Nov (results after the close) and fell 2.9% on 18 Nov.

rows.EpisodeTitle: Anthropic Goes Public, Nvidia in Crisis, Markets Tank, Open Source Crackdown?
rows.Speaker: Jason Calacanis
rows.Quote: And she ended the H200 sales to China.
rows.Claim: Interim CEO Colette Kress ended Nvidia's H200 sales to China, which Commerce had approved in January.
rows.Evidence: On the 17 Nov 2026 earnings call Kress said 'we are no longer shipping licensed Hopper data center products to China'. A BIS rule effective 15 Jan 2026 moved H200-class exports to China to case-by-case review with conditions. The board chair said on the same call it 'does not intend to reinstate Jensen as CEO'.
rows.Notes: He calls it elective; no report says it was ordered, though new US rules on foreign data centers serving Chinese customers came out the day before.

rows.EpisodeTitle: Anthropic Goes Public, Nvidia in Crisis, Markets Tank, Open Source Crackdown?
rows.Speaker: Jason Calacanis
rows.Quote: Nvidia is facing mounting legal issues. You predicted this, Chamath, SEC probe, class action lawsuits.
rows.Claim: Nvidia faces a reported SEC probe, a securities class action and DOJ investigations linked to Megaspeed.
rows.Evidence: The WSJ reported the SEC opened a civil investigation into whether Nvidia's disclosures misled investors. Rosen Law Firm filed a securities class action against Nvidia and Huang in federal court in San Jose on 10 Nov 2026. Semafor reported on 12 Nov that several DOJ probes could reach Nvidia, two of them concerning Megaspeed and Supermicro.
rows.Notes: The SEC and DOJ matters are reported investigations, not filed cases (see row 17).

rows.EpisodeTitle: Anthropic Goes Public, Nvidia in Crisis, Markets Tank, Open Source Crackdown?
rows.Speaker: Chamath Palihapitiya
rows.Quote: AMD is down 10 or 12 percent because somebody put out a short report that they were selling chips to China.
rows.Claim: AMD fell 10-12% on a short report alleging China sales.
rows.Evidence: On 19 Nov 2026 short seller Hunterbrook said AMD has significant exposure to Chinese companies under US export restrictions, including that blacklisted server maker IEIT received updated AMD firmware. AMD was down 6.8% at 11:16 a.m. ET and reportedly as much as 11% intraday.
rows.Notes: He calls AMD a trillion-dollar company; its market value was about $700bn the next day. Not the point.

rows.EpisodeTitle: Anthropic Goes Public, Nvidia in Crisis, Markets Tank, Open Source Crackdown?
rows.Speaker: David Friedberg
rows.Quote: Today, the largest fundraise in human history just took place. Anthropic in a day raised $85 billion.
rows.Claim: Anthropic's IPO was the largest fundraise ever, about $85bn in a day.
rows.Evidence: Anthropic's IPO raised $81.3bn ($107.3bn with the concurrent $26bn private placement), the largest IPO on record, ahead of SpaceX's $75bn base deal ($85.7bn with the over-allotment).
rows.Notes: $85bn is between the IPO alone and the total; the record, which is the point, stands. Same deal as row 1 (Jason).

rows.EpisodeTitle: Anthropic Goes Public, Nvidia in Crisis, Markets Tank, Open Source Crackdown?
rows.Speaker: Chamath Palihapitiya
rows.Quote: Ant is up from the IPO price 18 percent. You know what the only other company that's ripping right now is? Palo Alto Networks up 5.86 percent
rows.Claim: On a down day (S&P -1.4%), Anthropic was up 18% from its IPO price and Palo Alto Networks up about 6%.
rows.Evidence: Anthropic opened at $111.50 (+34%), hit $115.10 and closed at $97.17, up 17.1% on the $83 IPO price; the S&P 500 fell 2% that day. PANW traded up about 6% on 19 Nov after its results and Applied Compute deal.
rows.Notes: Intraday figures at taping can't be checked exactly; the close matches his Anthropic number. PANW's 19 Nov move comes from a live quote widget, not an article.

rows.EpisodeTitle: Anthropic Goes Public, Nvidia in Crisis, Markets Tank, Open Source Crackdown?
rows.Speaker: Chamath Palihapitiya
rows.Quote: these guys have to navigate three different committees on December 1st and 2nd.
rows.Claim: Huang and Nvidia must appear before three House committees on 1-2 December.
rows.Evidence: Huang agreed to appear before the House Foreign Affairs, Intelligence and China Select committees on 1 Dec 2026, and general counsel Tim Teter on 2 Dec, in transcribed, closed-door interviews.

rows.EpisodeTitle: Anthropic Goes Public, Nvidia in Crisis, Markets Tank, Open Source Crackdown?
rows.Speaker: David Friedberg
rows.Quote: It's like, call it 1% of the population, which explains why people remain pretty pessimistic, because they haven't really understood it yet.
rows.Claim: Only about 1% of people use AI tools every day, which explains public pessimism.
rows.Evidence: Pew (survey of 5,119 US adults, Feb 2026) found 24% use AI chatbots daily (12% several times a day, 4% almost constantly) and 49% use them at all.
rows.Notes: Off by more than an order of magnitude for the US, and the number is his explanation for pessimism. Pew measures US adults; he says 'the population'.

rows.EpisodeTitle: Anthropic Goes Public, Nvidia in Crisis, Markets Tank, Open Source Crackdown?
rows.Speaker: David Friedberg
rows.Quote: There has been no civil or criminal case that's been filed by the government against the company or by any of the government regulators against the company.
rows.Claim: No government civil or criminal case has been filed against Nvidia, and no official explanation of Huang's exit has been given.
rows.Evidence: As of 19 Nov 2026 the SEC matter was a reported investigation and the DOJ probes were reported, with Semafor saying there was no indication of criminal charges. The class action is private. Nvidia's announcements gave no reason for the resignation; its board said it had opened an independent inquiry.
rows.Notes: Consistent with row 11: probes reported, no government case filed.

rows.EpisodeTitle: Anthropic Goes Public, Nvidia in Crisis, Markets Tank, Open Source Crackdown?
rows.Speaker: David Friedberg
rows.Quote: It's why we don't see rising unemployment, because there's so much new stuff happening so quickly
rows.Claim: AI is not raising unemployment: the unemployment rate isn't rising.
rows.Evidence: BLS: the unemployment rate was 4.1% in October 2026 and 'has remained in a narrow range of 4.1 percent to 4.3 percent since March'; payrolls rose 165,000.
rows.Notes: Rated on the unemployment fact only; the cause (new AI industries absorbing workers) is his interpretation.

rows.EpisodeTitle: Anthropic Goes Public, Nvidia in Crisis, Markets Tank, Open Source Crackdown?
rows.Speaker: Chamath Palihapitiya
rows.Quote: To the extent Kevin Warsh wanted to cut, I don't think he's got much room. And if anything, he's going to hike.
rows.Claim: The Fed's next move under Warsh will be a hike, not a cut.
rows.Evidence: The FOMC raised rates by 25bp to 3.75-4.00% on 16 Sep 2026 and held on 28 Oct (two dissents for a hike). Futures priced a December hike at over 90% in mid-November.
rows.Notes: Rule (auto): Accurate if the FOMC raises the federal funds target range at any meeting from 20 Nov 2026 to 30 Jun 2027 before any cut; False if it cuts first; Misleading (partial) if the range is unchanged throughout. Hedged ('if anything'); scored on the stated lean. Source: Federal Reserve FOMC statements.

rows.EpisodeTitle: Anthropic Goes Public, Nvidia in Crisis, Markets Tank, Open Source Crackdown?
rows.Speaker: Chamath Palihapitiya
rows.Quote: I think that it's more likely that the tenure is at five and a half or six percent than it is at four and a half percent.
rows.Claim: The 10-year Treasury yield is more likely to head to 5.5-6% than to 4.5%.
rows.Evidence: The 10-year yield was about 5.07% on 19 Nov 2026, after a one-month high of about 5.15% on 13 Nov.
rows.Notes: Rule (auto): Accurate if the 10-year Treasury constant-maturity yield (FRED DGS10) closes at 5.25% or higher on 19 Nov 2027 (or the nearest trading day before); False if 4.75% or lower; Misleading (partial) in between. No deadline given; one-year window set.

rows.EpisodeTitle: Anthropic Goes Public, Nvidia in Crisis, Markets Tank, Open Source Crackdown?
rows.Speaker: Chamath Palihapitiya
rows.Quote: So I think you're going to have all kinds of pockets of opportunities to buy stuff much cheaper.
rows.Claim: Stocks are heading lower: risk-off, the S&P will offer much cheaper prices.
rows.Evidence: Said on 19 Nov 2026, when the S&P 500 fell about 2%. Later (1:13:09) he says he is 'principally risk-off' because 'the balance of motion in this market is down'.
rows.Notes: Rule (auto): Accurate if the S&P 500 closes at least 10% below its 19 Nov 2026 close on any day through 19 May 2027; False if it never does. No deadline given; six-month window set (he speaks of the next three or four months). Hedged ('maybe you can't be short'). Conflicts with row 22 (Jason); each scored on its own rule.

rows.EpisodeTitle: Anthropic Goes Public, Nvidia in Crisis, Markets Tank, Open Source Crackdown?
rows.Speaker: Jason Calacanis
rows.Quote: I think we're bouncing along the bottom, independent of like a crazy black swan type of event
rows.Claim: Stocks have bottomed; barring a black swan, they won't fall much further.
rows.Evidence: Said on 19 Nov 2026, when the S&P 500 fell about 2%.
rows.Notes: Rule (auto): Accurate if the S&P 500 never closes 10% or more below its 19 Nov 2026 close through 19 May 2027; False if it does. No deadline given; six-month window set. He excludes a 'black swan' (e.g. COVID): if a drop of 10%+ follows a sudden exogenous shock, it is noted and scored void. Conflicts with row 21 (Chamath).

rows.EpisodeTitle: Anthropic Goes Public, Nvidia in Crisis, Markets Tank, Open Source Crackdown?
rows.Speaker: Jason Calacanis
rows.Quote: We'll sit here in a year and the US ones will be somewhere in between DeepSeek and Kimi.
rows.Claim: Within a year, the best US open-weight models will rank among the leading Chinese ones, between DeepSeek and Kimi.
rows.Evidence: He ranks the US open models (Muse Spark, Nemotron, Reflection) behind Kimi, DeepSeek and GLM, with Mistral in between.
rows.Notes: Rule (auto): Accurate if on 19 Nov 2027 the top US-developed open-weight model scores above at least one of the best DeepSeek or best Moonshot (Kimi) open-weight models on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index; False if it scores below both. Related to AIA-20260904-14 (Jason: Nvidia open models surpass the best Chinese ones by end-2027).

rows.EpisodeTitle: Anthropic Goes Public, Nvidia in Crisis, Markets Tank, Open Source Crackdown?
rows.Speaker: Jason Calacanis
rows.Quote: I bet you this is what's going to come out. A bunch of rogue salespeople, you know, in a gray area, resellers on resellers, selling this, and it will wind up.
rows.Claim: Investigations will find that Nvidia chips reached China through rogue salespeople and resellers, not by Huang's design.
rows.Evidence: As of 19 Nov 2026 no official finding had been published. DOJ probes reportedly concern Megaspeed and Supermicro; Huang and Nvidia's general counsel give closed-door interviews to three House committees on 1-2 Dec.
rows.Notes: Rule (auto): Accurate if by 31 Dec 2027 an official finding (DOJ indictment or settlement, BIS penalty, SEC action, a House committee report, or the published result of Nvidia's board inquiry) attributes the diversion of Nvidia chips to China mainly to employees or third-party resellers acting without Huang's direction; False if one finds that Huang directed or knowingly facilitated it; void if no such finding is published by then.
